scope: Bounded ordinary DNS queries only; independent repeat of the 2026-10-24 06:34 JST trace (adversarial-review O10: the original had no raw capture and was never repeated). Raw dig output: artifacts/dns-authority-trace2-2026-10-27.raw.txt

observations.T3_T4_referral_repeatable: ns.lavoscore.org (authority of alice.poc.debiru.net) returns, for blog.alice.poc.debiru.net A (RD off), a REFERRAL with AUTHORITY NS ns-33.awsdns-04.com and ADDITIONAL A ns-33.awsdns-04.com -> 157.112.149.243. observations.T5_true_authority: Directly querying the independently reached authority 205.251.192.33 (real A of ns-33.awsdns-04.com) for blog.alice.poc.debiru.net A returns 162.43.9.153 (aa).
observations.T6_additional_endpoint: Directly querying the referral-ADDITIONAL-supplied endpoint 157.112.149.243 (PTR ns1.static.ne.jp) for the SAME name returns 85.131.199.2 (aa). Two authoritative servers disagree for one name; which answer a client gets depends on which endpoint the resolver reached.
observations.T7_ptr: 157.112.149.243 PTR = ns1.static.ne.jp (the PoC author's own host; O3: the emitter and the fake endpoint are attacker-controlled — cross-tenant emission remains unproven).
observations.T8_trace_local_iterator: dig +trace (local iteration) received the same referral from ns.lavoscore.org but did NOT use the ADDITIONAL address: it re-resolved ns-33.awsdns-04.com and reached 2600:9000:5300:2100::1, obtaining 162.43.9.153.
